headline: Attackers spent the day turning remote management software against the networks it administers, as N-able shipped a fourth emergency N-central hotfix for an exploited pre-authentication flaw, ConnectWise fought an unpatched ScreenConnect bug that now spreads malware worm-style, and MikroTik routers fell to a two-vulnerability chain.

emerging_trends.text: The software that managed service providers use to reach inside customer networks has become the fastest route to mass compromise, with N-central and ScreenConnect both under attack in the same week and one server exposing every network beneath it.
emerging_trends.topic_title: N-able Ships Fourth N-central Hotfix in Five Weeks

emerging_trends.text: Security products themselves keep landing on the target list, as Nightmare Eclipse follows its Kaspersky and CrowdStrike work with fresh proof-of-concept exploits that turn Nvidia and Avast software into a SYSTEM shell.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Nightmare Eclipse Drops CrowdStrike, Nvidia, and Avast Zero-Days

emerging_trends.text: Criminals increasingly walk past logins instead of cracking them, and JSCeal shows the pattern by replaying stolen browser session cookies straight into Google accounts without ever facing an authentication prompt.
emerging_trends.topic_title: JSCeal Steals Session Cookies to Walk Past Google Logins

topics.title: ScreenConnect File Transfers Carry Malware
topics.latest_developments: Huntress documented three unrelated intrusions in which backdoored ScreenConnect instances pushed a four-stage Visual Basic Script payload to every newly connected host, a worm-like spread that began with a Quick Assist tech-support scam, a phishing-delivered MSI installer, and a fake update; ConnectWise separately published temporary mitigations for the underlying file transfer flaw, confirmed it hits both its cloud service and on-premises installations, and promised a CVE identifier and a fix within the week.
topics.summary: ScreenConnect is the remote support and access tool that corporate IT departments and managed service providers use to take over user desktops, and the flaw abuses the file transfer built into live sessions. ConnectWise dated its advisory September 3, 2026; administrators should apply the interim mitigations now, audit connected clients, and update as soon as the patch ships.

sources.title: ConnectWise warns of new ScreenConnect flaw without patch
Attackers spread malware through ScreenConnect file transfers
Rogue ScreenConnect Clients Spread Four-Stage VBScript Chain to Newly Connected Hosts
Modified ScreenConnect Clients Used in Worm-Like Campaign

topics.title: N-able Ships Fourth N-central Hotfix in Five Weeks
topics.latest_developments: N-able assigned the maximum-severity pre-authentication remote code execution flaw CVE-2026-86218 and released Hotfix 4 for N-central 2026.3 on September 5, 2026, its fourth hotfix for the platform in five weeks, and told every on-premises operator running a build below 2026.3.1.14 to install it, including anyone who applied Hotfix 3 a day earlier.
topics.summary: N-central is the remote monitoring and management platform managed service providers use to administer customer machines, so one compromised server exposes every network beneath it. N-able's incident notice says attackers have exploited the flaw in the wild while its release notes call that unconfirmed; operators should patch immediately and hunt for intrusion.

sources.title: N-able Issues Fourth N-central Hotfix in Five Weeks for Unauthenticated RCE Flaw
N-able patches max severity N-central flaw amid ongoing attacks
N-able patches critical N-central zero-day exploited in the wild (CVE-2026-86218)

topics.title: Mathspace, Berlin, and Trezor Report Fresh Data Theft
topics.latest_developments: Mathspace, the online maths learning platform, disclosed over the weekend that attackers breached its Metabase internal reporting system and stole data on more than 1 million students, staff, and parents; Berlin's government said a second trove of stolen city data appeared online, with hackers publishing login credentials, while Germany's Federal Office for Information Security warned separately about the Rhysida cybercrime group; and Trezor put the total from the August breach at its fulfillment provider ShipMonk at 81,000 customers after adding 67,000 in the United States.
topics.summary: All three disclosures grew from intrusions at systems that sit behind the primary product—an internal analytics tool, city agency accounts, and a third-party shipping vendor. Customers and residents should treat exposed names, addresses, and credentials as material for targeted phishing, and reset any password reused elsewhere.

sources.title: Mathspace discloses data breach affecting over 1 million people
Berlin investigates new data leak after hackers publish stolen login credentials
Trezor data breach impact now reaches 81,000 customers

topics.title: Astra Reaches $20 Subscribers as OpenAI Automates Research
topics.latest_developments: OpenAI began rolling ChatGPT Astra out to $20-a-month Plus subscribers with no date announced for free users, and separately said it hit the goal it set last fall of fielding an automated research intern by September 2026, a system that completes well-defined research tasks under human direction that would occupy a skilled researcher for several days.
topics.summary: Astra is the first model OpenAI rates as crossing the critical cyber threshold under its Preparedness Framework; the company scored it at 100 percent on ExploitBench and made it refuse user requests for proof-of-concept exploits. OpenAI aims for a fully automated AI researcher by March 2028, and is testing a Writing Style feature that reads examples from a user's connected personal apps to imitate how they write.

sources.title: ChatGPT Astra is now rolling out to $20 Plus subscription
OpenAI just hit a milestone on the road to self-improving AI
ChatGPT can now connect to your personal apps to mimic writing style

topics.title: MikroTik RouterOS Flaws Chained to Hijack Routers
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer reported that attackers now chain two recently disclosed RouterOS vulnerabilities, rather than firing the SSH authentication bypass alone, to seize full control of MikroTik routers whose SSH service faces the internet.
topics.summary: MikroTik patched the SSH authentication bypass late last week after exploitation had already started, and the SANS Internet Storm Center told administrators to assume compromise because attackers add new accounts to the devices to survive the update. Anyone running RouterOS with SSH exposed should patch, audit the user list, and rotate credentials.

sources.title: Hackers exploit new MikroTik RouterOS flaws to hijack routers
Critical MikroTik Vulnerability - Patch Now

topics.title: Nightmare Eclipse Drops CrowdStrike, Nvidia, and Avast Zero-Days
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported that the researcher known as Nightmare Eclipse widened the release beyond the CrowdStrike Falcon Sensor bug published last week, dropping proof-of-concept exploits for unpatched privilege-escalation flaws in Nvidia and Avast software that each spawn a shell with SYSTEM privileges.
topics.summary: Nightmare Eclipse, also called Chaotic Eclipse, has now hit four security and driver vendors in eight days, following the HardBreacher exploit that forced a Kaspersky patch on August 31, 2026, and the FalconFlank exploit against CrowdStrike's macro-remediation routine. Endpoint software runs with the highest privileges on a machine, so defenders should watch vendor advisories for fixes and monitor for local escalation attempts.

sources.title: Nightmare Eclipse Drops CrowdStrike, Nvidia, Avast Zero-Day Exploits

topics.title: North Korean Crews Backdoor HAProxy in South Korea
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek tied the previously undocumented Linux toolkit that hides inside trojanized HAProxy load balancers to North Korean hackers, and named automotive and media organizations in South Korea as the targets of the long-term surveillance operation.
topics.summary: The toolkit, whose own debug strings call it ted, compiles a backdoor directly into the HAProxy binary, so the load balancer that fronts a web application also intercepts its traffic and serves altered pages to chosen visitors. Anyone running HAProxy in the region should verify binary integrity against vendor builds and review outbound connections from load balancers.

sources.title: North Korean Hackers Deploy New Linux Espionage Toolkit

topics.title: JSCeal Steals Session Cookies to Walk Past Google Logins
topics.latest_developments: Check Point Research published a teardown of JSCeal, malware compiled to V8 JavaScript bytecode that harvests credentials, watches the user, intercepts traffic, and replays stolen session cookies to enter Google accounts without triggering authentication.
topics.summary: JSCeal's operators wrap the payloads in javascript-obfuscator, protecting strings with RC4 and flattening control flow through proxy functions and operation wrappers to frustrate analysis. Defenders should treat stolen browser session cookies as a credential and shorten session lifetimes on Google accounts.

sources.title: JSCeal Malware Can Bypass Google Authentication Using Stolen Session Cookies

topics.title: Lenovo ID Hole Opened 5,000 Dropbox Accounts
topics.latest_developments: Graham Cluley, writing on Bitdefender's Hot for Security blog, detailed a flaw in Lenovo's login system that let hackers into roughly 5,000 Dropbox accounts that owners had linked to a Lenovo ID.
topics.summary: Lenovo laptop owners who connected Dropbox to their Lenovo ID for single-sign-on convenience inherited the weakness in Lenovo's authentication. Anyone who made that link should unlink the accounts, change the Dropbox password, and review recent file access.

sources.title: How a hole in Lenovo's login system let hackers walk into 5,000 Dropbox accounts

business_politics.title: Yen Hits a Six-Month High
business_politics.latest_developments: The yen touched 154.04 per dollar Monday, September 7, its strongest intraday level since late February, with the steepest part of the climb landing in the London morning as traders watched for signs of Japanese intervention.
business_politics.summary: The currency has recovered for a week as rate expectations shift, with markets pricing a Bank of Japan increase and, after last week's U.S. payrolls surprise, a Federal Reserve increase at the September 16 meeting; the same rate bets pushed German Bund yields higher and left copper and gold trading against a stronger tightening outlook.

sources.title: Yen surges to 6-month high as traders stay alert for signs of intervention
Yen Climbs to Six-Month High as Rate Outlooks Shift
Rise in German Bund Yields Almost Entirely Due to ECB Rate-Hike Prospects
Copper Rises on Supply Concerns Despite Rate-Hike Bets

business_politics.title: Brent Tops $97 as the U.S. and Iran Trade Strikes
business_politics.latest_developments: New strikes hit Saudi Aramco oil facilities at Jizan near the Yemeni border, a site Houthi rebels have targeted repeatedly, and Brent crude held above $97 a barrel through European afternoon trading Monday, September 7, after the United States and Iran exchanged a fresh series of strikes over the weekend.
business_politics.summary: The war continues to choke traffic through the Strait of Hormuz: European natural gas climbed more than 2% to just under 74 euros a megawatt-hour with Qatari supply flows severely disrupted, eurozone government bond yields opened higher ahead of the European Central Bank's rate decision Thursday, September 10, and Tehran announced it will raise petrol prices because war-driven shortages have made its fuel subsidies, among the cheapest in the world, unsustainable.

sources.title: Brent Tops $97 as U.S.-Iran Exchange Attacks
Saudi Aramco oil facilities hit in new strikes
Iran to raise petrol prices as US war triggers shortages
European Gas Climbs on LNG Supply Concerns Ahead of Winter
Oil Higher on Hormuz Escalation Amid Quiet Markets Due to Labor Day

business_politics.title: Germany Weighs Letting the AfD Govern
business_politics.latest_developments: Alternative for Germany co-leader Alice Weidel called Sunday's Saxony-Anhalt result a dream and set a target of 40% of the vote in Germany's next federal election, and the rival parties now must decide whether to hand the AfD the state government or lock it out.
business_politics.summary: The AfD finished well ahead of every rival in the September 6 Saxony-Anhalt election, the best showing in the party's history, and landed short of a majority in the state parliament, leaving Chancellor Friedrich Merz and the mainstream parties to choose between an awkward coalition of opponents and the first far-right state government in Germany since World War II.

sources.title: AfD co-leader vows to build on ‘dream result’ after victory in Saxony-Anhalt
After Far-Right Election Breakthrough, Germany’s Merz Faces Painful Dilemma
The Alternative for Germany has won its best-ever election result

business_politics.title: Beijing Recapitalizes Banks and Insurers
business_politics.latest_developments: Beijing said Monday, September 7, that it will inject $54 billion of fresh capital into state-controlled banks and insurers, widening the program to more institutions than the first round covered.
business_politics.summary: The infusion is China's second recapitalization of its financial system in less than two years and lands as growth momentum sputters; separately, China's foreign-exchange reserves edged higher in August on a weaker dollar and a surging trade surplus, renewing concern about the yuan's appreciation.

sources.title: China pumps $54bn into banks and insurers
Beijing to Inject More Than $50 Billion Into Banks, Insurers to Boost Growth
China’s Foreign Exchange Reserves Continue to Climb

business.title: Gasoline Sets a Labor Day Record
business.latest_developments: Iran announced a plan to create an exclusion zone around the Strait of Hormuz, WTAE reported Monday, September 7, as the national average price of regular gasoline reached an all-time Labor Day high for the holiday, three days after retail diesel set its own record at $5.85 a gallon.
business.summary: The war with Iran and refinery problems drive the increase, which lands on the last big driving weekend of the summer; WPXI and WTAE note the average for regular gasoline still sits below the all-time record of $5.02 a gallon set in June 2022.

sources.title: Fuel prices at record Labor Day high in US thanks to Iran War and refinery issues
Gas prices reach a new Labor Day high
Gas prices increase as Iran announces plan to create an 'exclusion zone' around Strait of Hormuz

business.title: East Ohio Street Booms in Deutschtown
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Monday, September 7, that investment along East Ohio Street has the corridor changing fast, four days after KDKA covered the campaign by Pittsburgh leaders to revive the district.
business.summary: East Ohio Street is the commercial spine of Deutschtown on Pittsburgh's North Side, where longtime merchants asked the city for help and now watch new businesses arrive; residents and owners told the Post-Gazette they want the growth to lift everyone already there rather than price them out.

sources.title: East Ohio Street is changing, even booming. Residents and business owners hope the new can lift all

around_town.title: Fetterman Texts Show Refusals of Constituent Work
around_town.latest_developments: KDKA reported Monday, September 7, that newly released text messages show U.S. Senator John Fetterman dismissing and at times refusing core constituent-service duties, a day after Fetterman told CNN that his curt text to Children's Hospital of Philadelphia leaders was a dumb joke.
around_town.summary: A former staffer confirmed the pattern to KDKA. The Pennsylvania Democrat's messages surfaced through Wall Street Journal reporting on his rejection of Children's Hospital of Philadelphia leaders' concerns about Medicaid cuts, coverage Fetterman has called a hit piece.

sources.title: Newly released Fetterman texts show a reluctance to perform constituent duties

around_town.title: Street Cameras Start Talking to AI
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Monday, September 7, that the automatic license plate readers posted along Pennsylvania streets increasingly feed artificial-intelligence systems, five days after Governor Josh Shapiro and state Treasurer Stacy Garrity called for a statewide ban on Flock cameras.
around_town.summary: Police departments across Pennsylvania query camera networks that photograph every passing plate and log vehicle movements into searchable national databases, a practice that has drawn privacy objections in Harrisburg and from communities around Pittsburgh.

sources.title: That street camera you just passed could be talking to AI

around_town.title: Blawnox Dresses Up Freeport Road
around_town.latest_developments: Blawnox officials are moving ahead with a beautification project for the borough's business district, TribLive reported Monday, September 7.
around_town.summary: The plan adds benches, tables, trash cans, and new signage along Freeport Road, the commercial strip that carries traffic through the small Allegheny River borough northeast of Pittsburgh.

sources.title: Upgrades coming to Blawnox business district

around_town.title: Sharpsburg Appoints Andrascik to Council
around_town.latest_developments: Sharpsburg council appointed borough resident Jon Andrascik as a councilman, TribLive reported Monday, September 7.
around_town.summary: Andrascik served on the Sharpsburg parks and recreation commission for a little more than a year and has coached Fox Chapel Area youth soccer and basketball for more than a decade.

sources.title: Sharpsburg appoints new councilman

events.title: Rib Fest Runs Through Labor Day
events.latest_developments: Judges crowned new barbecue champions over the weekend, with one fan favorite extending its winning streak, and the festival keeps serving through Labor Day, Monday, September 7, TribLive reported.
events.summary: The Acrisure Stadium Kickoff and Rib Festival sets up at Acrisure Stadium on Pittsburgh's North Shore, where competing rib vendors cook for prizes and for the crowd ahead of the Steelers' home opener against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, September 13.

sources.title: ‘Sauce is boss’: Rib Fest at Acrisure Stadium continues on Labor Day

around_teams.title: The Numbers Behind the Pirates' Fading Push
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette's Off The Bat column laid out Monday, September 7, the statistics that explain why a late-season Pirates surge remains unlikely.
around_teams.summary: The column builds its case around starting pitcher Paul Skenes, Marcell Ozuna, and Oneil Cruz as the Pirates play out September at PNC Park with their postseason odds shrinking.

sources.title: Off The Bat: If the Pirates don’t pull off a late-season stunner, they can blame these numbers

around_teams.title: Steelers and the Tight End Arms Race
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette wrote Monday, September 7, that head coach Mike McCarthy can put the Steelers one step ahead of the NFL's rush to stockpile tight ends by building the offense around two-tight-end personnel.
around_teams.summary: Pittsburgh opens the season against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, September 13, at Acrisure Stadium with Pat Freiermuth heading the tight end room; the Post-Gazette argues McCarthy's 12 personnel packages give quarterback Aaron Rodgers a way to dictate matchups as the rest of the league chases the same idea.

sources.title: How Mike McCarthy and the Steelers can get 'one step ahead' in the NFL's tight end arms race

team_usa.title: Belgium Balks at Infantino Over the Balogun Ruling
team_usa.latest_developments: The Belgian football federation said Monday, September 7, that it cannot support Gianni Infantino's bid for another term as FIFA president.
team_usa.summary: The federation cited transparency and governance concerns along with FIFA's handling of its decision to clear United States forward Folarin Balogun of a mandatory one-game ban at the 2026 World Cup, a call that drew objections from rival national federations.

sources.title: Belgium won't back Infantino bid, cite Balogun red

reading.summary: Newport marks the death of Wendell Berry at 92 at his home in Port Royal, Kentucky, where Berry farmed with traditional methods and wrote, and reads that life of place, slow work, and attention as the fullest case for what Newport calls the deep life.
